sources.title: Kambula Pride
sources.publisher: thewildlion.org (writer Sikander Hayat; compiled from public blogs/forums)
sources.what_it_adds: Pride-level lineage summary linking Majingilane -> Mhangeni -> Kambula -> Birmingham/Ndzhenga eras; secondary compilation, not primary Londolozi.

key_facts.claim: Kambula pride (also called Nstevu/Ntsevu by Londolozi) is six females born into the Mhangeni pride in 2013, sired by Majingilane males.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride

key_facts.claim: The six females had three brothers, the Mhangeni males, who went nomadic in 2016, the year the six females formed their own breakaway pride.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride / Mhangeni males

key_facts.claim: Kambula pride was said to have killed a Sparta pride female, the 'Tailless Tsalala female', and attacked members of their natal pride.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride / Tailless Tsalala
key_facts.confidence: low (conflicts with Mhangeni page, which says the Mhangeni pride killed BB)

key_facts.claim: 2016-2018: turnover of territorial males including Matshapiris, Southern Matimbas, Southern Avocas and the ageing Majingilane.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride

key_facts.claim: Birmingham males (four) intruded in 2017 and settled in 2018; five females gave birth to Birmingham-sired young mid-2018 to mid-2019; sixth female suspected infertile; pride grew to over 20.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride / Birmingham males

key_facts.claim: First Birmingham generation included six males and one female reaching adulthood; a second generation was born 2020-2021 but most cubs did not survive (Northern Avocas/Othawa male pressure).
key_facts.subject: Birmingham offspring

key_facts.claim: Late 2021: four Ndhzenga males invaded; Birmingham male 'Tinyo' disappeared (believed killed); last Birmingham male 'Nhenha' went nomadic.
key_facts.subject: Birmingham males / Ndzhenga males

key_facts.claim: As of 2025 pride split into two factions both under Ndzhenga control: main Kambula (5 adult females, 11 sub-adults, 4 cubs) and a 'Ntsevu' faction (3 adult females, 3 cubs).
key_facts.subject: Kambula / Ntsevu pride

sources.title: Mhangeni Pride
sources.what_it_adds: Origin of Mhangeni (Tsalala breakaway) pride and the Tailless Tsalala (BB) link; Majingilane two-generation reproduction.

key_facts.claim: Mhangeni pride (Tsalala breakaways) originated from four females born early-mid 2009 into the Tsalala pride, sired by Mapogo males, descended from the Tailless and Tailed Tsalala females.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni pride

key_facts.claim: In mid-2010 their grandmother, the original tailless female 'BB', left the Tsalala pride with the four sub-adult females to raise them away from the incoming Majingilane males, then later returned to her pride.
key_facts.subject: Tailless Tsalala (BB) / Mhangeni founders

key_facts.claim: The Mhangeni pride later encountered their grandmother on a kill and killed her.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni pride / BB
key_facts.confidence: low (conflicts with Kambula page attributing the killing to Kambula pride)

key_facts.claim: By late 2015 six young females and three young males left the Mhangeni pride; the six females later formed the Kambula pride, the males disappeared into Kruger. Majingilane sired a second generation born late 2015-mid 2016.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni / Kambula

key_facts.claim: Majingilane males died of old age in 2018; Mhangeni females left to find mates, abandoning 12 sub-adults (9 males, 3 females); two females returned; three males joined Nkuhuma pride late 2018 but died.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni 12

key_facts.claim: Birmingham males dominated Kambula pride but fathered some cubs with Mhangeni females (one female reached adulthood); Othawa male was pseudo-dominant, later killed (apparently by Birmingham males).
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni pride

key_facts.claim: Plains Camp males took over Mhangeni pride in early 2022, sired multiple litters; by mid-2025 the pride was 5 females and 4 young sub-adults and attracting the Nkuhuma male and Khanya.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni pride / Plains Camp males

sources.title: Majingilane Coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Majingilane origin, fight with Mapogo, prides sired and fate.

key_facts.claim: Five males; first appeared in Sabi Sands late 2009 as young nomads; names Darkmane, Scar Nose, Hip Scar, Golden Mane and a 'fifth Majingilane' killed by Mapogos.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane males

key_facts.claim: In mid-2010 Mapogo males Mr T and Kinky Tail killed one Majingilane (broke spine); that day the remaining four killed Kinky Tail; Mr T fled.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane / Mapogo

key_facts.claim: Majingilane first targeted Tsalala pride (which had Mapogo offspring); the tailless Tsalala female left with four young females to raise them away from the males.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane / Tsalala

key_facts.claim: By 2012 Majingilane had fathered at least 13 cubs in the Sparta pride (8 alive), 4 in Fourways and 6 in Styx, citing Londolozi.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane offspring

key_facts.claim: The Tsalala breakaway females (later Mhangeni pride) bred with Majingilane at maturity, producing the six females that became the Kambula pride plus three Mhangeni males.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane / Mhangeni / Kambula

key_facts.claim: Majingilane ousted the Selati males (2014), took over the Othawa pride and killed Selati offspring.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane / Othawa pride

key_facts.claim: Hip-Scarred male died 2017; the other three died in 2018 of old age.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane males

sources.title: Mapogo Coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Mapogo composition, origin in Sparta/Eyrefield pride, relationship to Nkuhuma, Styx, Tsalala prides.

key_facts.claim: Six males: five brothers from the Sparta/Eyrefield pride sired by the West Street males, plus older presumed half-brother Makulu. Names Makulu, Pretty Boy, Rasta, Dreadlocks, Mr T and Kinky Tail.
key_facts.subject: Mapogo coalition

key_facts.claim: Mapogos first claimed territory around March 2006; killed Nkuhuma male Blondie in 2007; ousted Styx's Roller Coaster male by mid-2009.
key_facts.subject: Mapogo / Nkuhuma / Styx

key_facts.claim: Mapogos fathered at least four Tsalala females that reached adulthood, plus litters in Sparta, Othawa, Ximunghwe, Ravenscourt and Sand River prides.
key_facts.subject: Mapogo offspring

key_facts.claim: Coalition split: Mr T and Kinky Tail east; Makulu, Pretty Boy, Rasta, Dreadlocks west.
key_facts.subject: Mapogo coalition

sources.title: Nkuhuma Pride
sources.what_it_adds: Nkuhuma coalition succession: Blondie/Dozie, Mapogo, Gijima(old), Matimba, Birmingham, Northern Avoca, Black Dam, Kambula males.

key_facts.claim: Pride officially named around 2006 in northern Sabi Sands under dominant males Blondie and Dozie; Mapogos killed Blondie in 2007.
key_facts.subject: Nkuhuma pride

key_facts.claim: Matimba males (six) arrived from the north in 2011; cubs born 2012 included Purple Eyes, Ridge Nose, Amber Eyes, Chela and Junior; the coalition split with Hairy Belly and Ginger as Southern Matimbas.
key_facts.subject: Nkuhuma / Matimba males

key_facts.claim: Birmingham males (five) are described as nephews of the Matimbas from the same natal pride; took over Nkuhuma peacefully in late 2015.
key_facts.subject: Birmingham males / Matimba males

key_facts.claim: Northern Avoca males (three) dominated Nkuhuma 2018-2023 after Birmingham moved south toward MalaMala.
key_facts.subject: Nkuhuma / Northern Avocas

sources.title: Styx Pride
sources.what_it_adds: Styx pride male sequence and generations.

key_facts.claim: Styx pride has roots in the early 1990s; males over time: Split Rock, Roller Coaster, Mapogo, Majingilane, Southern Matimbas, Birmingham, Avoca, Ndzhenga, then Gijima.
key_facts.subject: Styx pride

key_facts.claim: Majingilane fathered at least six cubs in Styx, producing a coalition of two males plus females.
key_facts.subject: Styx / Majingilane

key_facts.claim: By late 2020 Styx had three females, daughters of Roller Coaster males, Majingilane males, and one Birmingham-sired daughter.
key_facts.subject: Styx pride

sources.title: Ndhzenga Coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Ndzhenga members, origin and move north to Londolozi/Ntsevu pride.

key_facts.claim: Ndzhenga (N'waswitshaka) males: four; three from N'waswitshaka pride (Kruger), one from S79 pride. Names Amahle, Orange Eyes, Gore, Ubuso/crooked paw.
key_facts.subject: Ndzhenga males

key_facts.claim: Crooked-paw male died ~Feb 2023, Gore died May 2023; two remain.
key_facts.subject: Ndzhenga males

key_facts.claim: Remaining two moved north into Londolozi and MalaMala, ousted last Birmingham male, then the Ntsevu pride described as 'descendants of the very Birmingham Males they had replaced'.
key_facts.subject: Ndzhenga / Ntsevu pride / Birmingham

key_facts.claim: Ndzhengas also mated with the Kambula pride (four females born 2013, five from 2018); about 21 cubs born Nov 2022-Apr 2023.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride / Ndzhenga

sources.title: Gijima Coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Gijima coalition (new, 2022) vs the 2009-2011 'Gijima' males in Nkuhuma history; Msuthlu pride origin.

key_facts.claim: Current Gijima males: two young males active from 2022, originally a trio.
key_facts.subject: Gijima males

key_facts.claim: Gijimas took over Southern pride, Styx pride, and Msuthlu pride (Msutlu), formed by four Talamati breakaway females.
key_facts.subject: Gijima / Msuthlu pride

key_facts.claim: In mid-2025 Gijimas were seen frequently around Londolozi and MalaMala.
key_facts.subject: Gijima males

sources.title: Plains Camp Coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Plains Camp males parentage and conflicts.

key_facts.claim: Two males born 2017, half-brothers to the two Mantimahle males, sired by five Mantimahle males in Kruger.
key_facts.subject: Plains Camp males

key_facts.claim: They became dominant over Ximunghwe pride and Nkuhuma breakaways; conflict with Ndzhenga in 2024.
key_facts.subject: Plains Camp males

sources.title: Othawa Pride
sources.what_it_adds: Othawa pride succession; Othawa male parentage.

key_facts.claim: Othawa male born 2015, sired by Majingilane, from a Mapogo-descended lioness; later dominant over Mhangeni pride until death 2021; sister 'Sassy'.
key_facts.subject: Othawa male

key_facts.claim: Selati males ruled Othawa 2012-2014 before Majingilane takeover.
key_facts.subject: Othawa pride

sources.title: The Majingilane Lions of Sabi Sands
sources.what_it_adds: Independent corroboration of Majingilane cub counts, origin and fate.

key_facts.claim: Five brothers originally; one killed in 2010 by Mapogo males; four remained.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane

key_facts.claim: Cubs sired: Tsalala 11 (3 surviving), Fourways 4 (3), Styx 6 (5), Sparta 13 (8); total 34, 19 surviving.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane offspring

key_facts.claim: Held most of Londolozi area, about 26,676 ha at peak; Hip-Scar died first, Golden Mane died after buffalo injury; Dark Mane and Scar-Nose ended by old age.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane

sources.title: Mapogo lion coalition
sources.what_it_adds: Encyclopedia-style corroboration of Mapogo and Majingilane clash, Selati kill of Mr T. Uncited sections flagged by Wikipedia.

key_facts.claim: Mapogo originated from the Sparta/Eyrefield Pride; six members Makulu, Pretty Boy, Rasta, Dreadlocks, Kinky Tail, Mr T; controlled Sabi Sand 2006-2012.
key_facts.subject: Mapogo coalition

key_facts.claim: Mr T killed by the Selati coalition (four) on 16 March 2012.
key_facts.subject: Mr T / Selati

key_facts.claim: Majingilane (five) entered Mapogo territory in June 2010; one killed, then Kinky Tail killed by the other four.
key_facts.subject: Majingilane / Kinky Tail

sources.title: 21 Lions and Cubs. The Kambula Pride Seen at Umkumbe
sources.what_it_adds: Lodge corroboration that Kambula parentage is Majingilane x Mhangeni/Tsalala breakaways and cubs sired by Birmingham males.

key_facts.claim: Six Kambula females are the offspring of the Majingilane males and the Mhangeni/Tsalala breakaways.
key_facts.subject: Kambula pride

key_facts.claim: Kambula cubs were sired by the Birmingham ('Birmingham/Gowrie') males; 21 lions counted together.
key_facts.subject: Kambula / Birmingham

sources.title: The Lions of Londolozi
sources.what_it_adds: Londolozi-specific 2019 snapshot: Ntsevu pride with 12 cubs, Tsalala female.

key_facts.claim: Ntsevu pride toured Londolozi with 12 cubs; 21 lions seen at one time.
key_facts.subject: Ntsevu pride

key_facts.claim: The remaining Tsalala lioness was the only female born to the Tailed Tsalala lioness; her three brothers dispersed into Kruger; she denned near Manyeleti River where she was born.
key_facts.subject: Tsalala pride

sources.title: Holding the Line: The Nkuhuma Lionesses Part 1
sources.what_it_adds: Independent Nkuhuma history.

key_facts.claim: Nkuhuma pride first found late 2006 at Buffelshoek; mid-2007 nine lionesses, about 16 cubs, dominant males Blondie and Dozie.
key_facts.subject: Nkuhuma pride

sources.title: The Birmingham Pride: Lions of Greater Kruger
sources.what_it_adds: Disambiguation: Birmingham Pride (Ngala/Timbavati) is distinct from the Birmingham male coalition.

key_facts.claim: The Birmingham Pride is a separate lioness family from the Birmingham male coalition; they share deep roots in the same Timbavati corner but are different animals.
key_facts.subject: Birmingham pride vs Birmingham males

sources.title: Lion dynamics and territorial shifts at Lion Sands
sources.what_it_adds: Southern Sabi Sand 2024 corroboration: Gijima, Mkhuhlu(Nkuhlu) males, Styx, Southern, Msuthu prides.

key_facts.claim: Gijima males mated with Styx females; Mkhuhlu (four) males pushed on Lion Sands western boundary in 2024.
key_facts.subject: Gijima / Nkuhlu males

sources.title: Lions of Sabi Sands Game Reserve - Prides and Coalitions
sources.what_it_adds: Closest thing to a structured lion database: 14 prides and 11 coalitions with short descriptions; Oct 2026 'community map' entries; thin and unverified.

key_facts.claim: Lists prides: Imbali, K7&K9, K8&K10 (Kambula BA), Mhangeni, Msuthlu, Nkuhuma, Ntsevu, Othawa, Sand River, Southern, Styx, Torchwood, Tsalala, Bateleur; coalitions Gijima, Mapogo, Ndzenga, Nkuhlu, Nkuhuma 2016 & Talamati male, Nkumati, Plains Camp, Kambula males, Styx & Floppy Ear Nomads, Young N'waswitshaka, Young Torchwood.
key_facts.subject: Sabi Sand prides/coalitions

key_facts.claim: Ntsevu pride: 3 adult females and 3 subadults sired by the Ndzhenga males.
key_facts.subject: Ntsevu pride

key_facts.claim: Mhangeni pride dominated by Nkuhuma 2016 male and the Talamati male; subadults sired by Plains Camp males.
key_facts.subject: Mhangeni pride

key_facts.claim: Tsalala pride reduced to a single adult female, in Gijima territory; Msuthlu pride sired by Gijima males.
key_facts.subject: Tsalala/Msuthlu

key_facts.claim: Ndzenga males: two remaining (Eorenji and Amahle) aged 10; Gore and Ubisuso died.
key_facts.subject: Ndzhenga males

key_facts.claim: K7&K9 and K8&K10 are Kambula offshoots; K7&K9 cubs sired by Ndzhenga.
key_facts.subject: Kambula offshoots

sources.title: The Leopards of Londolozi (and leopards.londolozi.com lineage/dynasties)
sources.what_it_adds: Evidence that Londolozi maintains structured leopard lineage pages (WP types leopard n=87, lineage n=7) but NO equivalent for lions.

key_facts.claim: leopards.londolozi.com exposes WP REST types 'leopard' and 'lineage' (7 lineages: Little Bush, River Female, Unknown, Short Tail Female, Saseka Female, Sunset Bend, Mother Leopard); no lion type exists.
key_facts.subject: Londolozi site structure

sources.title: Londolozi blog 'Lions' category and tags (metadata only)
sources.what_it_adds: Taxonomy metadata only (bodies not read): category 'Lions' has 862 posts; tag 'Lion' 1099; tags for Kambula lioness, gijima male lions, Birmingham lion, Nkuhuma pride, Lion Dynamics (26) etc.

key_facts.claim: Blog category Lions (id 3325) holds 862 posts; the blog is the only lion archive on Londolozi sites.
key_facts.subject: Londolozi blog

gaps: No dedicated lion family tree / profile database exists on londolozi.com, photography.londolozi.com, leopards.londolozi.com or blog.londolozi.com: www sitemap has no lion pages; WP REST types on blog/photography have no lion/pride type; leopards site has leopard and lineage types for leopards only.
Only Londolozi lion archive is blog.londolozi.com category Lions (862 posts) and tags (e.g. /tag/nkuhuma-pride/, /tag/lion-dynamics/); these are being processed separately.
Third-party sources conflict: thewildlion.org says Mhangeni pride killed the Tailless Tsalala (BB) but its Kambula page says Kambula pride did so; Londolozi blog should be treated as authoritative.
thewildlion.org says Kambula is 'also known as Ntsevu by Londolozi' and later splits a Ntsevu faction; naming mapping between Kambula and Ntsevu needs Londolozi blog confirmation.
Nomenclature clash: 'Gijima' males (2009-2011 northern duo) vs Gijima males (2022 southern duo); 'Birmingham Pride' (Ngala/Timbavati) vs Birmingham males.

Facebook pages (Tsalala.Lions, Birmingham.Male.Lions, Nkuhuma.Lions) and Greater Kruger Wiki (kruger.fandom.com) could not be fetched (login/402/blocked); Leopard Hills, Luxury Safari Company, Arathusa blocked (403/406/Cloudflare).
No source found giving individual lioness names/mothers for Kambula, Ntsevu, Msuthlu pride members; wild-guide.org entries are community-sourced and thin.
No external source examined for Mapogo/Matimba/Nkumati male fathers at Londolozi beyond summaries; Nkumati males only listed on wild-guide (2 males, western, Oct 2026).
